task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req033-snapshot-store.md -- read the actual file, not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary. CODE-DESIGNER reports: no tenant_id derivation needed (instance_definition_snapshots has no tenant_id column, tenant-scoped via :prefix only -- confirmed directly against the migration, verify this yourself too); create/3(instance_id, definition_id, opts) and get_by_instance_id/2(instance_id, opts) (note the arity differs from the requirement text's literal 'create/2'/'get_by_instance_id/1' because opts[:prefix] is required -- confirm this deviation is called out explicitly and is justified, not silently introduced); one Repo.transaction/2 closure (not Ecto.Multi) doing a FOR SHARE-locked read of process_definitions then an on_conflict: :nothing insert then a re-select; idempotent-no-op reading chosen for AC2 with stated reasoning; AC4 satisfied entirely by REQ-027's already-shipped on_delete: :nothing (no SnapshotStore code involved). Three open questions flagged: OQ-1 (cross-tenant definition_id indistinguishable from nonexistent), OQ-2 (idempotency keys only on instance_id, not checking definition_id agreement across retries -- flagged as structurally similar to a pattern REQ-025 treated as unacceptable), OQ-3 (FOR SHARE lock mode unverified against unreachable R-Co source). Run the standard checklist (every AC has a concrete design element, function signatures fully specified including error cases, error handling shape stated, cross-module deps listed, NO implementation code -- grep for def/defmodule/Repo.insert(/Repo.transaction(/Ecto.Multi./on_conflict:/lock( used as literal code rather than named-in-prose) fresh, independently.
acceptance_criteria: every REQ-033 acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element
function signatures (including the opts[:prefix] arity deviation from the requirement's literal text) fully specified with error cases
no implementation code present -- prose/pseudocode only
open questions (OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-3) stated explicitly, not silently resolved

result.summary:
PASS. Read lib/letflow/design/req033-snapshot-store.md directly in full (564 lines), docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-033 entry (lines 1514-1554), and independently re-read the three shipped artefacts the design cites rather than trusting its quotations: lib/letflow/definitions/instance_definition_snapshot.ex (full file), lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex (full file), and priv/repo/migrations/20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs (full file).

CHECK (a) every AC maps to a design element, no TBD/deferral -- PASS. Section 11's traceability table maps all 5 REQ-033 acceptance criteria to concrete sections (AC1->S6.2 L1/L2, AC2->S5+S6.2 L2/L3+S8 item2, AC3->S4.2 @spec+S6.4, AC4->S7 (REQ-027's shipped on_delete: :nothing, no SnapshotStore code involved -- verified directly against the migration file, which does declare on_delete: :nothing with no ON DELETE clause emitted, matching the design's claim), AC5->S8 item1. Grepped the whole file for TBD|to be determined|to be decided|to be implemented later|not yet specified|left as an exercise|placeholder -- zero matches.

CHECK (b) function signatures fully specified including error cases -- PASS. Section 4.1 gives create/3's full @spec (instance_id :: Ecto.UUID.t(), definition_id :: Ecto.UUID.t(), opts :: [prefix: String.t()]) :: {:ok, InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.t()} | {:error, create_error()}; Section 4.2 gives get_by_instance_id/2's full @spec with its 2-tag error union; Section 4.3 gives the complete create_error() type union with one distinct tag per named failure mode (:missing_prefix, :definition_not_found, Ecto.Changeset.t(), term() catch-all) plus explicit prose on what is deliberately absent from the union (no SnapshotAlreadyExists-equivalent tag, no instance_id_conflict tag) and why. The arity deviation is independently verified as real and clearly called out, not silently introduced: Section 2.1 states in its own heading 'On the requirement text's create/2/get_by_instance_id/1 naming' and explains create/3 and get_by_instance_id/2 carry one more positional parameter each (opts[:prefix]) than the requirement's shorthand, with the reasoning (no sensible default tenant schema, opts[:prefix] required not optional) and an explicit warning against ELIXIR-DEV misreading the requirement literally.

CHECK (c) error handling shape stated -- PASS. Every path is explicitly {:ok, _} | {:error, tag}, never an implicit/bare return; Section 6.1-6.4's pseudocode states the exact tag returned at each branch point (P0 -> {:error, :missing_prefix}, L1 no-row -> {:error, :definition_not_found}, L3 always succeeds).

CHECK (d) cross-module dependencies listed -- PASS. Section 10's table lists ProcessDefinition (read-only, locked), InstanceDefinitionSnapshot (create_changeset/2 reuse + on_conflict layered at call site), Letflow.Repo (every call passes prefix: opts[:prefix] explicitly), and the not-yet-built S3/EE-01 caller (explicitly marked out of scope, not silently omitted).

CHECK (e) no implementation code present -- PASS. Grepped the full file for real Elixir/Ecto executable syntax used as literal code rather than named in prose: '^\s*def ', '^\s*defp ', 'defmodule Letflow.Definitions.SnapshotStore do', 'Repo.insert(', 'Repo.transaction(', 'Repo.get(', 'Ecto.Multi.', 'Ecto.Query.lock(' -- zero hits anywhere in the file. Also grepped for '|>' (pipe-chain code) -- zero hits. All 7 fenced code blocks in the file are: one shell command transcript (the R-Co unreachability check, lines 95-98), two @spec type signatures (lines 201-207, 230-235), one @type union (lines 247-265), and three numbered-prose pseudocode blocks (P0 at 338-342, the transactional L1-L3 phase at 356-405, get_by_instance_id at 435-446) that describe algorithm shape in full sentences (e.g. 'Compose an Ecto.Query against ProcessDefinition: WHERE id == ^definition_id, with the query's lock option set to...') and name option keywords/function references in prose (on_conflict: :nothing, conflict_target: :instance_id, Repo.insert/2) rather than writing a literal compilable call or pipeline -- matching the same named-function-reference-only convention independently confirmed as already validator-approved for req025-event-append.md's Section 6 (checked handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-01b-code-design-validator.json's own PASS re-validation, which describes and accepts the identical style: 'named-function-reference style only ... as a name, not a call with real arguments chained into a pipeline').

CHECK open questions stated, not silently resolved -- PASS. Section 9 lists OQ-1 (cross-tenant definition_id indistinguishable from nonexistent -- flagged for SECURITY-REVIEWER, reasoned but not asserted as confirmed against PD-08's primary text), OQ-2 (idempotency keys only on instance_id, not definition_id agreement across retries -- explicitly flagged as structurally similar in shape to a pattern REQ-025's Section 3 treated as unacceptable for tenant_id, with the distinction and similarity both stated rather than glossed over), OQ-3 (FOR SHARE lock mode taken from the requirement text's own quotation, not independently verified against unreachable R-Co source). None of the three is silently resolved as fact.

Independent fact-checks against shipped code (not the design's own quotations): instance_definition_snapshot.ex confirmed to have no tenant_id field, @primary_key {:instance_id, :binary_id, autogenerate: false}, exactly the fields the design's L2 attrs list uses (instance_id, definition_id, definition_name, definition_ver, graph), create_changeset/2 as the only changeset exposed, unique_constraint(:instance_id, ...) and foreign_key_constraint(:definition_id, ...) both present as the design describes. process_definition.ex confirmed to carry field(:tenant_id, Ecto.UUID) and no @schema_prefix, matching the design's Section 3 claim that this module reads but never writes that column. The migration confirmed: instance_definition_snapshots created inside 'if prefix() do', no tenant_id column anywhere in the table, definition_id reference uses on_delete: :nothing (falls through to Postgres NO ACTION, no ON DELETE clause emitted) -- matching AC4's traceability claim exactly. REQ-027 (the dependency both tables ship under) confirmed status: done in docs/requirements.yaml.

Net: all five checklist items pass, the arity deviation and all three open questions are independently confirmed present and adequately justified/flagged rather than silently resolved, and every factual claim about shipped code the design makes was independently re-verified against the actual files rather than trusted from the design's own quotations. Design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to build create/3 and get_by_instance_id/2 from without inventing behavior.
